answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may claim rewards or vote. A newcomer can forge identities cheaply, but each must tie up real capital; if linked accounts collude or double-claim, a challenge can prove the conflict and slash their deposits. This makes a Sybil attack costly in proportion to its influence, while a relic reputation earned over time can raise trusted agents’ weight without letting fresh accounts inherit it. Slashing also creates a ripple: attackers risk losing funds, and honest participants gain reason to report abuse.
